advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Move the INSTANCE_ID_CACHE directory creation so it also runs when only IID (not REGION) is valid, or hoist the mkdir out of the REGION case.
evidence: The mkdir is gated on REGION being valid (inside the `*)` branch of `case "$REGION"`), but the IID write is independent of REGION.
advisory.finding: The instance-id cache write at line 273 runs whenever IID matches `i-*`, but the `mkdir -p` that creates the INSTANCE_ID_CACHE parent directory only runs inside the `case "$REGION"` valid branch (line 269). When REGION is empty/invalid (IMDS region miss, cache miss) yet IID is valid, the directory is never created and the cache write silently fails, so the instance-id cache never populates on a cold start where only the region read failed.
advisory.suggested_fix: Add `mkdir -p "$(dirname "$INSTANCE_ID_CACHE")" 2>/dev/null || true` immediately before the line-273 IID write, or hoist both mkdirs above the two case statements.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Handle REGION_CACHE values without a slash when deriving the default INSTANCE_ID_CACHE path (e.g. use dirname or guard the slashless case).
evidence: For REGION_CACHE without a slash, `${REGION_CACHE%/*}` == REGION_CACHE, yielding `<REGION_CACHE>/probe-instance-id`.
advisory.finding: The INSTANCE_ID_CACHE default `${REGION_CACHE%/*}/probe-instance-id` mis-derives the path if REGION_CACHE is set to a value with no `/`: `%/*` leaves a slashless string unchanged, so the default becomes `<REGION_CACHE>/probe-instance-id`, treating the region-cache filename as a directory.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Add a test where IMDS returns a fresh IID (e.g. i-fresh999) and assert INSTANCE_ID_CACHE is written with that value on the main probe path.
evidence: Test curl stub returns exit 1 for `*169.254.169.254*`, so IID is never populated from IMDS and the write branch never executes (tests/scripts/test_observability_timeout_9313.py:696-698).
instance_cache is only pre-seeded and read back (tests/scripts/test_observability_timeout_9313.py:690,737); no assertion reads INSTANCE_ID_CACHE after a run to confirm a fresh IID was written.
Named violating input: IMDS succeeds with IID=i-fresh999 and REGION valid, then the run must write i-fresh999 into INSTANCE_ID_CACHE — no test drives this.
advisory.finding: The newly added instance-id cache WRITE path is untested: the diff adds `case "$IID" in i-*) printf '%s\n' "$IID" >"$INSTANCE_ID_CACHE"` (and the added mkdir of its dirname), but the only new test forces IMDS to fail and merely pre-seeds/reads the cache, so a fresh instance id is never persisted or asserted. A run where IMDS returns a fresh `i-fresh999` would not verify the value is written to INSTANCE_ID_CACHE, so a regression that stops writing (or writes the wrong value) would go undetected.
scenarios: A future edit drops or mistypes the instance-id cache write; the reuse test still passes because it pre-seeds the cache, so the cache silently stops being refreshed.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Move the INSTANCE_ID_CACHE mkdir -p to run before the unconditional instance-id write (line 273) so the write does not depend on the REGION-valid branch.
evidence: 178:INSTANCE_ID_CACHE="${INSTANCE_ID_CACHE:-${REGION_CACHE%/*}/probe-instance-id}" — decouplable from REGION_CACHE via env override
advisory.finding: The INSTANCE_ID_CACHE parent directory is only ensured (mkdir -p) inside the REGION-valid branch (lines 266-272), but the instance-id cache write at line 273 runs unconditionally. When REGION is empty/invalid while IID is valid AND INSTANCE_ID_CACHE is configured to a directory other than REGION_CACHE's (the two only coincide by default), the write to INSTANCE_ID_CACHE silently fails because its directory was never created, so the instance-id cache never populates in that state.
scenarios: IMDS returns a valid instance-id but the region query misses/garbles, and operators point INSTANCE_ID_CACHE at a different directory than REGION_CACHE via env.
advisory.suggested_fix: Ensure the instance-id cache directory exists in the same guard that writes it, e.g. before line 273: `case "$IID" in i-*) mkdir -p "$(dirname "$INSTANCE_ID_CACHE")" 2>/dev/null || true; printf '%s\n' "$IID" >"$INSTANCE_ID_CACHE" 2>/dev/null || true ;; esac`.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Bound cached-metadata reuse (freshness/host-identity) or document why a stale InstanceId dimension is acceptable during IMDS misses.
evidence: Cache validity check is only a syntactic i-* prefix match; there is no check that the cached id belongs to the running host and no staleness/TTL bound (ABSENCE rationale).
advisory.finding: Cached instance-id/region are reused with no freshness bound or host-identity check; a persisted cache file (e.g. on a reused/attached EBS volume, or a stale /var/lib/rebar after an instance replacement) will cause CloudWatch metrics to be published under a STALE InstanceId dimension, mislabeling the current host's health as another instance's.
scenarios: Instance replaced but the same /var/lib/rebar contents persist, or a volume carrying probe-instance-id is reattached to a different host, while IMDS is briefly unreachable at probe start.
